source.title: Open problems for the superKdV equations

accepted.question_text: For N = 2 supersymmetric extensions of the Korteweg-de Vries equation with an odd Poisson structure, can one construct integrable extensions in which the bosonic fields do not evolve independently of the fermionic fields, but instead the bosonic evolution equations contain genuine fermionic interaction terms?

evidence.quote: A new N = 2 super KdV equation with an odd Poisson structure has been found recently in [7] but the resulting equations are somewhat less interesting in that the bosonic fields do not couple to the fermions in their time evolution. It would be of interest to see whether there are other 'odd' integrable extensions displaying fermionic interactions in the bosonic evolution equations.

accepted.question_text: Can one find an integrable deformation of the N = 1 supersymmetric KdV system whose conserved quantities reproduce the fermionic nonlocal conservation laws that arise from the fourth-root structure of the Lax operator and behave as Poisson square roots of the usual local bosonic conservation laws?

evidence.quote: The sKdV equation represents the first example of an integrable system for which nonlocal conservation laws arise in such a clean form. In that respect, we introduce the first open problem (OP): OP-1: Find an integrable deformation that reproduces the fermionic nonlocal conservation laws.

accepted.question_text: For each of the three integrable N = 2 super KdV equations SKdV_a with a = -2, 1, and 4, can one find an integrable Gardner-type deformation whose conserved quantities reproduce the infinite tower of conservation laws generated from the corresponding Lax formulation?

evidence.quote: Although there exists a Miura transformation, there are no known integrable (i.e., Gardner-type) deformations of it. This leads us to: OP-2: Find an integrable deformation for SKdV−2,1,4 that reproduces their conservations laws.

accepted.question_text: For the integrable N = 2 super KdV equations SKdV_{-2} and SKdV_4, what is the precise relation between their two independent towers of fermionic nonlocal conservation laws and the corresponding Lax operator, given that the Lax operator has two distinct fourth roots but those roots have not been connected to the fermionic conserved quantities?

evidence.quote: For a = −2, 4, there are two independent towers of fermionic nonlocal conservations laws [18]: in each case, the first one is ... However, although the Lax operator has two distinct fourth roots, these have not yet been related to these fermionic conservation laws: OP-3: For SKdV−2,4, find the relation between the fermionic nonlocal conservation laws and the Lax operator.

accepted.question_text: Why does the integrable N = 2 super KdV equation SKdV_1 fail to produce infinite towers of fermionic conservation laws, even though the first fermionic conserved quantities exist and the presence of two supersymmetries would naturally suggest extended fermionic conservation-law hierarchies?

evidence.quote: The existence of these fermionic conservation laws is natural in that there are two supersymmetries. On the other hand, for the a = 1 case, the first fermionic laws (3.9) do not generate infinite towers: they are isolated. OP-4: Why there are no infinite towers of fermionic conservation laws for SKdV1?

accepted.question_text: Does the integrable N = 2 super KdV equation SKdV_1 admit a bihamiltonian structure, despite being one of the rare classical integrable systems not known to be bihamiltonian, unlike the SKdV_{-2} and SKdV_4 cases whose first and second Hamiltonian operators are known?

evidence.quote: The SKdV−2,4 equations are both bihamiltonian ... In that respect, the SKdV1 stands as one of the rare example of classical integrable system which is not (known to be) bihamiltonian. OP-5: Is SKdV1 bihamiltonian?

accepted.question_text: Why are there exactly three integrable N = 2 supersymmetric Korteweg-de Vries extensions, and is there an underlying Lie-algebraic explanation for this threefold classification, for example one connected to the existence of three classical algebras?

evidence.quote: OP-6: Why is there exactly three integrable N = 2 super KdV extensions? Is there an underlying Lie algebraic interpretation for this threefold way (i.e, is this related to the existence of the three classical algebras)?

accepted.question_text: Is it possible to formulate the Painlevé analysis directly in superspace for supersymmetric integrable systems, so that the superspace formulation itself supports the same structural insights that the ordinary Painlevé test gives for integrable equations, including access to objects such as Bäcklund transformations and Lax operators?

evidence.quote: There are further general questions that could be formulated in relation with super integrable systems. As stressed here, these equations are naturally formulated in superspace. Over the years, it became clear that a lot of structure is contained in the Painlevé test: for instance its truncation leads to Backlund transformations and the Lax operator [20]. Yet, no Painlevé analysis has been done directly in superspace. OP-7: Is it possible to formulate the Painlevé analysis in superspace?

accepted.question_text: Can Darboux transformations and corresponding solution-generating techniques be developed for the N = 2 super KdV equations, extending the existing N = 1 Darboux-transformation results to the N = 2 setting where the paper states that no such work had yet been done?

evidence.quote: Moreover, little is known concerning the solutions of super integrable systems. The Darboux transformation in the N = 1 case has been worked out in [21] but nothing has been done at this point concerning the N = 2 cases.
